Title: Opening balances match the opening ledger
Preconditions: A temporary database has the three fictional users.
Steps: Sign in as demo_zhang and compare the balance with the ledger view and the password hash.
Expected: Balance is 10000.00 CNY (1000000 fen) and equals the opening credit. The passphrase is stored as an Argon2id hash.

Title: A deposit posts one credit
Preconditions: demo_zhang is signed in with 10000.00 CNY.
Steps: Deposit, then read the balance and the new ledger row.
Expected: Balance increases by 10050 fen. One credit. Books stay consistent.

Title: A withdrawal posts one debit
Steps: Withdraw and check the ledger direction.
Expected: Balance decreases by 2000 fen. One debit. Books stay consistent.

Title: A transfer updates both balances and both ledger rows
Preconditions: Mingyuan Zhang and Wanqing Li are open.
Steps: Transfer to SIM-1002 and read both balances and the two postings.
Expected: Zhang loses 8880 fen and Li gains 8880 fen. One debit and one credit. The supply of money is unchanged. The response omits the receiver balance.

Title: A transfer appears in both histories
Preconditions: Zhang and Qinian Wang are open.
Steps: Transfer to Wang and query both activity lists.
Expected: Same entry id. Zhang sees Transfer out. Wang sees Transfer in. Counterparty and amount agree.

Title: Transferring the whole balance keeps both sides consistent
Steps: Wang transfers the entire balance to Zhang.
Expected: Wang is at 0. Zhang increases by that amount. The sum of all balances is unchanged.

Title: The receiving account number ignores case
Steps: Transfer using a lowercase account number and read Li's balance.
Expected: The credit lands on SIM-1002. Li increases by 1 fen.

Title: A withdrawal over the balance is rejected
Steps: Withdraw more than the balance and count debits.
Expected: insufficient_funds. Balance unchanged. No new debit.

Title: A transfer over the balance is rejected
Steps: Li tries to send more than that to Zhang.
Expected: Both balances stay the same.

Title: A malformed recipient is rejected
Steps: Submit an empty account, a short account, and accounts containing SQL text.
Inputs: 1.00 CNY and several invalid account strings.
Expected: invalid_recipient every time. Balance unchanged. The accounts table remains.

Title: An unknown recipient is rejected
Steps: Transfer to a well-formed account that does not exist.
Expected: 404 recipient_not_found. Balance unchanged.

Title: A transfer to oneself is rejected
Steps: Transfer to that same account.
Expected: self_transfer. Balance unchanged.

Title: The minimum amount of 0.01 CNY posts
Steps: Deposit one fen.
Expected: Balance becomes 10000.01 CNY.

Title: Zero is rejected on deposit, withdrawal, and transfer
Steps: Send 0, 0.00, and integer 0 to each write endpoint.
Expected: non_positive_amount. Balance unchanged.

Title: Negative amounts are rejected
Steps: Send negative strings and a negative integer to each write endpoint.
Expected: non_positive_amount. Balance unchanged.

Title: More than two decimal places are rejected
Steps: Send three-decimal amounts to each write endpoint.
Expected: overprecision. Balance unchanged.

Title: Non-finite amounts are rejected
Steps: Send JSON NaN and Infinity, then the same tokens as strings.
Expected: nonfinite_amount. Balance unchanged.

Title: Invalid amount strings and types are rejected
Steps: Send scientific notation, thousands separators, a plus sign, blanks, a boolean, null, and a list.
Expected: invalid_amount. Balance unchanged.

Title: JSON floats are rejected and JSON integers mean whole CNY
Steps: Send JSON number 10.5, then JSON integer 2.
Expected: The float returns amount_must_be_string. The integer posts 200 fen.

Title: Amounts above the cap are rejected
Steps: Send an over-cap amount to each write endpoint.
Expected: amount_overflow. Balance unchanged.

Title: A deposit that would pass the balance cap is rejected
Steps: Deposit up to the cap, then try 0.01 CNY more.
Inputs: The gap to 10^15 fen, then 0.01 CNY.
Expected: The second call is amount_overflow. The balance stays at the cap and the books still match.

Title: Mixed deposits, withdrawals, and transfers still match the ledger
Preconditions: Zhang and Li use separate sessions.
Steps: Zhang deposits, withdraws, and transfers to Li. Li then withdraws.
Expected: Both balances equal the running ledger. The totals view agrees.

Title: Withdrawing the exact balance succeeds
Steps: Withdraw 5000.00, then 0.01.
Expected: The first call leaves 0. The second is insufficient funds.

Title: A repeated deposit posts only once
Steps: Deposit twice with the same Idempotency-Key.
Expected: The second call is a replay. The entry id matches. The balance increases by 1234 fen once.

Title: A repeated transfer posts only once
Steps: Transfer twice with the same key in the JSON body.
Expected: Both balances change once. There is one transfer row.

Title: The same key with a different amount conflicts
Steps: Deposit 1.00 and then 2.00 with the same key.
Expected: 409 idempotency_conflict. Only the first amount is kept.

Title: A failed withdrawal does not consume the idempotency key
Steps: Withdraw an excessive amount with a key, then withdraw 1.00 with that same key.
Expected: The first call is insufficient funds. The second succeeds and is not a replay.

Title: Idempotency keys are isolated per user
Preconditions: Zhang and Li are signed in separately.
Steps: Each deposits 1.00 with the same key string.
Expected: Both succeed, neither is a replay, the entry ids differ, and each balance increases by 100 fen.

Title: Concurrent withdrawals do not overdraw
Steps: Two connections withdraw the full balance at the same time.
Inputs: Two withdrawals of 10000.00 CNY with different keys.
Expected: Exactly one succeeds and one is insufficient funds. The balance is 0. There is one debit.

Title: Query parameters cannot read another account
Steps: Request the account endpoint with Zhang's account number and user id.
Expected: The response is still Li's SIM-1002 and 5000.00 CNY.

Title: Activity is isolated to the signed-in user
Preconditions: Zhang and Li are signed in separately.
Steps: Zhang deposits a unique note. Li reads activity and also passes Zhang's account number.
Expected: Li does not see the note. Zhang does.

Title: Account reads require a session
Steps: Call health, account, activity, and profile.
Expected: Health is 200 and marked as a simulation. The others are 401.

Title: Sign-out invalidates the session
Steps: Sign out, then read the account.
Expected: Sign-out succeeds. The account call is then 401.

Title: A deposit without a session is rejected
Steps: Deposit with CSRF and an idempotency key.
Expected: 401. No deposit row is stored.

Title: Missing CSRF does not post
Steps: Deposit through the API without CSRF, then submit the page form without CSRF.
Expected: Both calls are 403. The balance is unchanged.

Title: Sign-in rotates the CSRF token
Preconditions: A CSRF token was issued before sign-in.
Steps: Sign in, deposit with the old token, then deposit with the new token.
Expected: The old token is 403. The new token succeeds. The balance increases by 100 fen once.

Title: An injected fault after the write rolls the entry back
Preconditions: Fault injection is enabled only in this test.
Steps: Deposit with the fault header, check the response and books, then retry without the fault.
Expected: 500 with no internal details. Balance and rows unchanged. The retry succeeds.

Title: The fault header is ignored unless tests enable it
Steps: Deposit with the fault header.
Expected: The deposit succeeds and the balance increases.

Title: SQL injection in the sign-in form does not authenticate
Steps: Try classic, UNION, and boolean-style injection strings as the username and passphrase, then sign in normally.
Inputs: OR 1=1, AND 1=1, AND 1=2, UNION SELECT, comments, and DROP TABLE text.
Expected: Every attempt is 401. Three users remain and the tables are still there.

Title: SQL text in a transaction form is stored as data
Steps: Deposit a note that contains DROP TABLE and UNION SELECT text, then send hostile amounts and account numbers.
Inputs: A note with DROP TABLE and UNION SELECT text, plus invalid amounts and recipients.
Expected: One real deposit. The note is stored as text. Hostile fields are rejected. The accounts table remains. The balance increases by 100 fen.

Title: Activity escapes HTML in a note
Steps: Deposit a script-tag note and open the page and the JSON API.
Expected: The page escapes the tag. The API returns the original text.

Title: The session cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite
Steps: Sign in and inspect Set-Cookie.
Expected: HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax are present. Secure is absent in this local mode.

Title: Unknown users and wrong passphrases get the same message
Steps: Sign in as an unknown user and as demo_zhang with a wrong passphrase.
Inputs: An unknown username and a wrong passphrase.
Expected: Both are 401 with the same message. The message does not say whether the user exists.

Title: The pages sign in, move money, ignore a duplicate post, and sign out
Preconditions: A temporary ledger and the fixture passphrase.
Steps: Use the rendered forms to sign in, deposit twice, withdraw, transfer, read activity, and sign out.
Expected: The duplicate deposit does not post twice. The balance returns to 10000.00. Li gains 10.00. Activity redirects after sign-out.

Title: Sign-in ignores an external next address
Preconditions: The sign-in page has issued CSRF.
Steps: Sign in with an external next parameter.
Expected: The redirect stays on the in-site home page.

Title: Error responses do not leak stack traces
Steps: Request a missing path, bad paging, invalid JSON, and a disallowed method.
Inputs: limit=abc and a body of not-json.
Expected: 404, 400, 400, and 405, with no traceback or database error type.

Title: The browser signs in and shows the balance
Preconditions: Chrome or Chromium can be discovered. A temporary server is up.
Steps: Open sign-in at 1440 pixels, sign in, read the balance, then check 390-pixel overview and deposit.
Inputs: The fictional user and the temporary fixture passphrase.
Expected: The page shows the simulation warning and 10,000.00 CNY. The page does not scroll sideways. If no browser is found, the case is skipped and the reason is kept.

Title: The browser deposits, withdraws, transfers, and checks activity
Preconditions: Chrome or Chromium can be discovered.
Steps: Use the pages to deposit, withdraw, and transfer, then open activity and read the receiver balance from the database.
Expected: The visible balance returns to 10,000.00. Activity contains the three notes. Li's balance increases by 700 fen.

Title: The README lists the accounts and does not contain a passphrase
Steps: Check names, balances, passphrase instructions, the reset command, and tracked files.
Expected: The three usernames and opening balances are documented. The passphrase is described, not printed. Secret files are not tracked.

Title: The catalog matches the test functions
Preconditions: The tests directory can be parsed.
Steps: Parse every test_ function and compare it with this catalog.
Expected: The function names match exactly.

Title: The reset command rebuilds a database only after confirmation
Preconditions: BANK_DATABASE points at a temporary file.
Steps: Run without --yes, then with --yes, and sign in.
Inputs: A temporary database path and the fixture passphrase in the environment.
Expected: Without --yes the file remains. After --yes the three users and opening balances are restored.

Title: Sign-in is English and images are stored locally
Preconditions: The sign-in template and static files are present.
Steps: Open sign-in and check language, names, balances, and local files.
Expected: lang=en, Linden Ledger, the romanized names, unchanged balances and account ids, and a real local JPEG and font.

Title: Signed-in pages use English chrome
Preconditions: A temporary ledger exists for demo_zhang.
Steps: Sign in and open overview, deposit, withdrawal, transfer, activity, and the passphrase page.
Expected: Each page says it is not a bank. The opening balance is still 10,000.00 CNY. Old Chinese navigation words are absent. Original images are on the pages.

Title: The passphrase policy rejects incomplete and weak values
Preconditions: The policy requires 12 characters and four character classes.
Steps: Validate short, incomplete, repeated, sequential, keyboard, common, and identifier-based values, then a fixture that meets the rules.
Inputs: Several rejected passphrases and one accepted fixture passphrase.
Expected: Every rejection uses the same policy message. The message does not say a value is on a denylist. The accepted value is returned unchanged.

Title: Lockout blocks the correct passphrase until the cooldown ends
Preconditions: The lockout threshold is 3 for this case.
Steps: Fail sign-in three times, try the correct passphrase, move the lock into the past, and sign in.
Inputs: A wrong passphrase, then the correct one.
Expected: The message stays generic. The correct passphrase is rejected while locked. After the stored lock time is in the past, sign-in succeeds.

Title: Stored passphrases are distinct Argon2id hashes
Preconditions: Three fictional users were seeded with different fixture passphrases.
Steps: Read the three hashes from the temporary database.
Expected: Each hash starts with the Argon2id marker, the three hashes differ, and none equals its passphrase.

Title: Changing the passphrase updates the hash and ends other sessions
Steps: Reject a weak replacement and a reuse, then change the passphrase from one session.
Inputs: The current fixture passphrase and a new fixture passphrase.
Expected: The other session is rejected. The old passphrase no longer signs in. The new one does. The stored hash changed and is still Argon2id.

Title: A shared seed passphrase is refused
Preconditions: Two accounts are given the same configured passphrase.
Steps: Initialize a temporary database.
Inputs: A passphrase map with a repeated value.
Expected: Initialization raises and does not write the demo passphrase file.

Title: A weak seed passphrase is refused
Preconditions: One configured passphrase fails the policy.
Steps: Initialize a temporary database.
Inputs: A passphrase map with one weak value.
Expected: Initialization raises the policy error and does not write the demo passphrase file.

Title: A 100-character note is stored on a deposit
Steps: Deposit 0.01 CNY with a 100-character note and read activity.
Expected: The deposit posts and activity stores all 100 characters.

Title: A 101-character note is rejected
Steps: Deposit with a 101-character note and count deposit rows.
Expected: invalid_note. The balance is unchanged and no deposit row is stored.

Title: Surrounding spaces do not count toward the note limit
Steps: Deposit a note of 100 characters with spaces on both ends.
Inputs: Two spaces, 100 T characters, two spaces.
Expected: The stored note is the 100 T characters.

Title: A null byte is removed from a note
Steps: Deposit a note that contains a null byte between two words.
Inputs: The text alpha, a null byte, and beta.
Expected: The stored note is alphabeta.

Title: A null note is stored as an empty string
Steps: Deposit with a JSON null note.
Expected: The deposit posts and the stored note is empty.

Title: A numeric note is rejected
Steps: Deposit with a JSON number as the note.
Expected: invalid_note. The balance is unchanged.

Title: An 8-character idempotency key is accepted
Steps: Deposit with a key of exactly 8 characters.
Expected: The deposit posts once and is not a replay.

Title: An 80-character idempotency key is accepted
Steps: Deposit with a key of exactly 80 characters.
Expected: The deposit posts.

Title: A 7-character idempotency key is rejected
Steps: Deposit with a key of 7 characters.
Expected: idempotency_key_required. The balance is unchanged.

Title: An 81-character idempotency key is rejected
Steps: Withdraw with a key of 81 characters.
Expected: idempotency_key_required. The balance is unchanged.

Title: An idempotency key with a space is rejected
Steps: Transfer with a key that contains a space.
Inputs: Key with a space, 1.00 CNY, SIM-1002.
Expected: idempotency_key_required. The balance is unchanged.

Title: A deposit without an idempotency key is rejected
Steps: Post a deposit with neither a header nor a JSON key.
Expected: idempotency_key_required. The balance is unchanged.

Title: A withdrawal accepts the idempotency key in JSON
Steps: Withdraw with the key only in the JSON body.
Expected: The withdrawal posts once. The balance falls by 125 fen.

Title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same key does not debit twice
Steps: Withdraw 2.00 twice with one key.
Expected: The second response is replayed. The balance falls by 200 fen once. One withdrawal row exists.

Title: A failed transfer leaves the idempotency key unused
Steps: Transfer to an unknown account with a key, then transfer to SIM-1002 with that key.
Expected: The first call is recipient_not_found. The second posts and is not a replay.

Title: A transfer that would push the receiver over the cap is rejected
Preconditions: Li is filled to the balance cap. Zhang still has the opening balance.
Steps: Zhang transfers 0.01 CNY to SIM-1002.
Expected: amount_overflow names the receiving balance. Both balances stay where they were.

Title: A transfer may land the receiver exactly on the cap
Preconditions: Li is one yuan below the cap.
Steps: Zhang transfers 1.00 CNY to Li, then tries 0.01 CNY more.
Expected: The first transfer posts and Li is at the cap. The second is amount_overflow.

Title: Two full-balance transfers cannot both post
Steps: Two connections transfer that whole balance at the same time, one to Li and one to Wang.
Inputs: Two transfers of 10000.00 CNY with different keys.
Expected: Exactly one succeeds. Zhang is at 0. Only one receiver changes. The sum of balances is unchanged.

Title: Concurrent transfers from two senders both post
Preconditions: Zhang and Wang can each afford their transfer to Li.
Steps: Both send to SIM-1002 at the same time.
Inputs: 100.00 CNY from Zhang and 50.00 CNY from Wang.
Expected: Both succeed. Li increases by 150.00 CNY. The books still match.

Title: Two deposits with one key post once
Steps: Two connections deposit 1.00 CNY with the same key at the same time.
Expected: One result is the original post and the other is a replay. The balance increases by 100 fen once.

Title: A unique-key collision with no stored result returns conflict
Preconditions: Zhang is open. The idempotency insert is forced to raise IntegrityError and no key row is left behind.
Steps: Deposit through that forced collision.
Expected: conflict 409. The balance is unchanged and the books still match.

Title: A unique-key collision returns the stored result when the fingerprint matches
Preconditions: The idempotency insert is forced to raise IntegrityError after a matching key row is made visible.
Steps: Deposit through that forced collision.
Expected: The call returns the stored deposit marked replayed. The balance is unchanged.

Title: A unique-key collision with a different fingerprint conflicts
Preconditions: The idempotency insert is forced to raise IntegrityError and the stored fingerprint does not match.
Steps: Deposit through that forced collision.
Expected: idempotency_conflict 409. The balance is unchanged.

Title: Activity limit 1 returns the newest entry
Preconditions: Zhang has deposited after the opening entry.
Steps: Request activity with limit 1.
Expected: One row, and it is the deposit.

Title: Activity offset 1 skips the newest entry
Preconditions: Zhang has one deposit after the opening entry.
Steps: Request activity with limit 1 and offset 1.
Expected: The row is the opening entry.

Title: Activity limit above 100 is rejected
Steps: Request activity with limit 101.
Expected: invalid_paging.

Title: Activity offset above 100000 is rejected
Steps: Request activity with offset 100001.
Expected: invalid_paging.

Title: The profile endpoint ignores another user's query
Steps: Request the profile with Zhang's user id and username in the query string.
Expected: The body is Li, SIM-1002, and it has no balance.

Title: The opening entry is labeled Opening
Preconditions: Zhang is signed in and has not posted yet.
Steps: Read activity and find the opening row.
Expected: kind_label is Opening, direction is In, and the amount is 10000.00.

Title: A transfer is Out for the sender and In for the receiver
Preconditions: Zhang and Li are signed in separately.
Steps: Zhang transfers 1.50 CNY to Li and both read activity.
Inputs: 1.50 CNY to SIM-1002 with note labels.
Expected: Zhang sees Transfer out. Li sees Transfer in. The note matches.

Title: One decimal place posts the right number of fen
Steps: Deposit the amount 1.5.
Expected: The entry is 150 fen and the balance increases by 150 fen.

Title: A leading zero in the yuan amount is rejected
Steps: Deposit 01.00.
Expected: invalid_amount. The balance is unchanged.

Title: Spaces around an amount are ignored
Steps: Withdraw an amount with spaces around it.
Expected: The withdrawal posts 250 fen.

Title: Spaces around an account number still find the receiver
Steps: Transfer to a lowercase account number wrapped in spaces.
Expected: Li increases by 2 fen.

Title: A numeric recipient is rejected
Steps: Transfer with a JSON number as the account.
Expected: invalid_recipient. The balance is unchanged.

Title: The deposit page requires a session
Steps: Open the deposit page.
Expected: The response redirects to /login.

Title: The activity page requires a session
Steps: Open the activity page.
Expected: The response redirects to /login.

Title: A signed-in user opening sign-in is sent to the overview
Steps: Open the sign-in page.
Expected: The response redirects to /.

Title: A web withdrawal over the balance stays on the form
Preconditions: Zhang is signed in with 10000.00 CNY.
Steps: Submit the withdrawal form for 10000.01.
Expected: The form returns the insufficient-funds message. The balance is unchanged.

Title: A web transfer to an unknown account stays on the form
Steps: Submit the transfer form to SIM-9999.
Expected: The form says the account does not exist. The balance is unchanged.

Title: Mismatched passphrase confirmation does not change the hash
Steps: Submit the passphrase form with two different new values.
Expected: The page says they do not match. The stored hash is unchanged.

Title: Sign-out without CSRF keeps the session
Steps: Post sign-out with an empty body, then open the overview.
Expected: Sign-out is rejected. The overview still shows the opening balance.

Title: The posted-balance line appears after a second entry
Preconditions: Zhang is signed in and has only the opening entry.
Steps: Open the overview, deposit 1.00 on the form, and read the overview again.
Expected: The line is absent before the deposit and present after it.

Title: A wrong CSRF token rejects a deposit
Steps: Deposit with a token that is not the session token.
Expected: csrf_failed. The balance is unchanged.

Title: A username longer than 64 characters does not sign in
Steps: Sign in with a 65-character username.
Expected: login_failed. The account endpoint stays unauthorized.

Title: A non-text passphrase does not sign in
Steps: Sign in as demo_zhang with a JSON number as the passphrase.
Expected: login_failed. No session is created.

Title: The wrong current passphrase does not change the hash
Steps: Change the passphrase and supply a current value that is not the account passphrase.
Inputs: A wrong current value and a replacement value.
Expected: login_failed. The stored hash is unchanged.

Title: Pages send the simulation security headers
Steps: Open the sign-in page and read the response headers.
Expected: nosniff, DENY, same-origin, frame-ancestors none, the simulation header, and no-store are present.

Title: A three-step transfer chain conserves the balances
Preconditions: All three fictional accounts are open.
Steps: Zhang sends 10.00 to Li, Li sends 4.00 to Wang, and Wang sends 1.00 to Zhang.
Expected: Each balance matches that chain and the sum is unchanged.

Title: The note limit counts characters
Steps: Deposit a 100-character Unicode note, then a 101-character one.
Inputs: 100 then 101 copies of one CJK character.
Expected: The first is stored. The second is invalid_note. Only one deposit row exists.

Title: A stale expected balance does not update the account
Steps: Ask the balance guard to write a new balance while claiming a different current balance.
Expected: conflict 409. The stored balance is unchanged.

Title: The balance guard rejects a result outside the allowed range
Steps: Ask the balance guard to write one fen above the cap, then a negative balance.
Expected: Both calls are amount_overflow. The stored balance is unchanged.

Title: A wrong passphrase stays on the sign-in page
Preconditions: Chrome or Chromium can be discovered. A temporary server is up.
Steps: Open sign-in and submit demo_zhang with a wrong passphrase.
Inputs: Username demo_zhang and a wrong passphrase.
Expected: The browser stays on the sign-in page, shows the generic failure, and does not show the balance or the submitted passphrase.

Title: A local env file fills only names that are not already set
Preconditions: A temporary env file is used. No passphrase is written.
Steps: Load comments, a blank value, a quoted value, an existing name, and a new name.
Inputs: A temporary env file with non-secret markers.
Expected: The existing name is kept, the new name is loaded, the quoted value loses its quotes, and the blank value is ignored.

Title: The session key comes from an override, the environment, a file, or a new file
Preconditions: The session file path is a temporary file. The value is not printed.
Steps: Resolve an override, an environment value, the testing default, an existing file, an empty file, and a missing file.
Inputs: Markers in the test process and a temporary file.
Expected: Each source wins in that order. Testing mode does not write a file. A missing file is created and read back.

Title: A private-file write still returns the key when chmod fails
Preconditions: chmod is forced to raise. The file is temporary.
Steps: Generate a session key into the temporary file.
Expected: The key is still written and returned. The error is ignored.

Title: Seed passphrases come from the environment or a file, and tests refuse to invent one
Preconditions: The credentials path is temporary. Values are not printed.
Steps: Resolve from the environment, then from a file, then refuse under testing, then generate outside testing.
Inputs: Per-account environment names and a temporary credentials file.
Expected: Environment and file values are used. Testing mode raises and writes nothing. Outside testing, three distinct values are written to the temporary file.

Title: A configured seed map must name every demo account
Preconditions: The app config has a seed map with one account missing.
Steps: Resolve seed passphrases for all three usernames.
Inputs: A map that only names demo_zhang.
Expected: Resolution raises and does not write a credentials file.

Title: SQLMap evidence targets only the local coursework app
Preconditions: The sanitized SQLMap summary and outcome file are already in the repository.
Steps: Read the outcome file and the summary. Check every target, technique, and the CVSS field.
Expected: Every target is http://127.0.0.1. UNION and blind techniques are recorded. A CVSS score is present only when the outcome says a parameter was injectable.

Title: GitHub Actions runs pytest and uploads the reports
Preconditions: The workflow file is in the repository.
Steps: Read the workflow and check the events, the pytest command, and the artifact paths.
Expected: Pull requests and main run pytest with coverage, an HTML report, and Allure results. The workflow does not contain a seed passphrase setting.
